scope: project-owned Python verification, evidence, and test programs

roles.cmake.version: Resolve CMake and request only its version.
roles.cmake.configure: Configure this project into a fresh directory below .build with the two declared options.
roles.cmake.build: Build only a directory below .build with parallel scheduling.
roles.ctest.run: Run CTest only against a directory below .build with failure output enabled.
roles.git.head: Read whether HEAD resolves.
roles.git.praxis_head: Observe the exact Praxis Git HEAD used by the run.
roles.git.praxis_status: Observe the Praxis working-tree state without mutation.
roles.python.collector: Run exactly the project RF-A0 collector against the built probe and the current run directory.
roles.python.praxis_validator: Run exactly the current sibling Praxis governed-project validator against SRF.
roles.probe.run: Run the built srf-runtime-probe with an experiment file below .build and ephemeral loopback port.

delegation_boundary: CMake legitimately launches the configured compiler and linker as children of the build system. This policy bounds commands launched directly by project-owned Python code; it does not pretend to enumerate CMake's internal build graph.
limitations: Static inspection proves only the subprocess call-site structure understood by the gate.
Executable and argument allowlisting bounds direct launch authority but cannot prove semantic behavior of an allowed external program.
The operating system and pre-existing tool installations remain environmental authorities outside the repository.
